newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine Senate rejects bid to question ministers.
newsitem.headline: Argentine Senate rejects bid to question ministers.

text.p: Argentina's Senate late on Wednesday rejected a motion filed by the opposition Radical that two cabinet ministers should be questioned over corruption cover-up allegations.

The charges were made Tuesday in New York by former Economy Minister Domingo Cavallo. He alleged Interior Minister Carlos Corach and Justice Minister Elias Jassan often meddled in court investigations and gave secret orders to prosecutors and judges.
But the ruling party Peronist caucus, which has an absolute Senate majority, turned down the motion to call the ministers in for questioning after a long debate Wednesday night.

President Carlos Menem has stood by his cabinet and dismissed the statements of Cavallo, whom he sacked nearly three months ago after a running battle between the outspoken minister and the Peronist old guard over the issue of government-linked corruption. Cavallo first denounced "mafias" in state customs and postal services more than one year ago.
Last week Menem vowed to wage war on corruption after a judge cracked a massive smuggling ring in Customs.
